top_findings.title: pyproject declares a build backend that does not exist in any setuptools release, so the package cannot be installed
top_findings.evidence: pyproject.toml:3 sets build-backend = "setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend". Reproduced in a temp copy: `python -m build --wheel --no-isolation` against setuptools 82.0.1 fails with `BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'` / `ERROR Backend 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' is not available.` The module is absent in setuptools 58.0.4 and 82.0.1 (setuptools has no `backends` subpackage at all); only `setuptools.build_meta` exists. Tests still pass because pytest imports the package from the repo root rather than from an install, so the mechanical gate never exercises the backend.
top_findings.suggestion: Set build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta". Without this, `pip install .` fails and the declared `brazilian-soccer-mcp` console script (pyproject.toml:24) can never be created.

top_findings.title: search_players silently discards the name/nationality/position filter when the club filter is set and the prior filters matched nothing, returning the club's whole roster instead of no results
top_findings.evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp/query_engine.py:238 — `players = [p for p in players if p.id in player_ids] if players else found`. The `if players` guard is falsy exactly when a preceding filter (name at :232, nationality at :234) has already narrowed the list to empty, so the code falls back to `found` (every player at the club) and the earlier filter is dropped. Reproduced against the real QueryEngine with a stub graph: `search_players(name="NoSuchPlayerXYZ", club="Flamengo")` returned `Found 2 player(s) matching criteria: 1. Gabriel Barbosa ... 2. Everton Ribeiro ...` instead of "No players found matching the criteria." (`search_players(nationality="Argentina", club="Flamengo")` correctly returns no players, because that intermediate list is non-empty — the bug needs an empty intermediate.)
top_findings.suggestion: Drop the ternary and always intersect: `players = [p for p in players if p.id in player_ids]`. The `else found` branch has no valid case — an empty `players` list should stay empty. Add a test for a non-matching name combined with a real club.
